incentives.name: Sales and use tax exemption for qualifying data centers
incentives.what: Exempts purchases or leases of machinery, equipment, and normal operating repair or replacement parts (economic life of one year or more) by a qualifying data center or an occupant of one, used in operating the data center.

incentives.name: MIDA project-area tax terms (Stratos)
incentives.what: In a MIDA project area the authority set a 0.5% energy use tax (normally 6%), a 1.2% flat property tax with rebates, and personal property tax rebates for the Stratos data center; the developer keeps 80% of tax revenue at the county rate.

laws_and_bills.name: S.B. 132 (2025) Electric Utility Amendments
laws_and_bills.what: Sponsors Sen. Scott Sandall / Rep. Colin Jack. Creates Utah Code 54-26: alternative processes to serve large electrical loads, lets large-scale generation providers serve large load customers when the utility can't, closed private generation systems, transparency rules to protect retail customers, and requires the PSC to study a large load flexible tariff. (Enrolled copy read; governor signature not checked.)

laws_and_bills.name: Gov. Cox executive order on data centers (May 2026)
laws_and_bills.what: Executive order setting a 'higher bar' / guardrails for data center development (details not read).

laws_and_bills.name: 2027 bill files: define large-scale data centers; environmental impact studies; incentive and water guidelines
laws_and_bills.what: Economic Development and Workforce Services Interim Committee (Sen. Ann Millner) opened a bill file to define large-scale data centers; Rep. Doug Owens plans an environmental impact study requirement; Rep. Paul Cutler drafting guidelines for data centers seeking state incentives, including water limits in the Great Salt Lake and Colorado River basins.

local_rules.what: 180-day moratorium on new data centers and data center power plants on unincorporated land, unanimous; does not apply to Stratos (land-use authority transferred to MIDA for 50 years).
Unanimous 180-day temporary land use regulation barring new or incomplete applications for data centers, data center power plants and utility-scale solar.
180-day moratorium on data center development in unincorporated areas, 6-0; no applications received.
Ordinance 26-12, temporary land use regulation prohibiting development and construction of data centers and data center power plants, adopted 2026-06-30.
Unanimous 180-day pause (2026-07-07) on applications, permits and licenses for data centers, data center power plants and related digital infrastructure; no pending applications.
Resolution 2026-04, unanimous 180-day moratorium on land use applications for data centers and data center power plants (including nuclear).
180-day moratorium on data center development, 4-0; no proposal pending.

Industrial 4 zone for data centers adopted late 2025: air-cooled or closed-loop cooling required, light rules, air permits before city approval, council discretion on large sites. Juab County adopted temporary moratoriums while updating land use law (details not given).
City council denied 7-0 a rezoning for a 66,000 sq ft data center (B+F Timpanogos Tech Center, 6-10 MW) in East Bay.
